title: Sustainable Finance and ESG for Firms
summary: An eight-module programme giving firms the tools to manage climate and ESG risks, prepare credible disclosures and transition plans, and avoid greenwashing.
intro: This training programme equips risk, compliance, investment and sustainability staff to manage climate and ESG risks, make credible sustainability claims and evidence their approach, seeing the firm the way a supervisor does.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip firms with a practical understanding of how climate and wider ESG risks affect their business and customers, and how supervisors expect those risks to be governed, managed and disclosed. Participants leave able to integrate climate risk into risk management, prepare credible disclosures and transition plans, and avoid greenwashing.
sections.What It Covers: Climate risk management, scenario analysis, transition plans, ISSB-style disclosures, product labelling and greenwashing, ESG data, stewardship, and governance of sustainability risks.
Intended Audience: Risk, compliance and sustainability professionals in regulated firms
Portfolio managers, product developers and stewardship teams
Finance, reporting and senior management staff responsible for sustainability disclosures
Learning Objectives: Explain how climate and ESG risks translate into financial and prudential risks for the firm
Apply climate scenario analysis and integrate results into risk management
Design a credible transition plan with targets, metrics and governance
Prepare sustainability disclosures aligned with ISSB and TCFD frameworks
Identify and prevent greenwashing in products, labels and marketing
Evaluate ESG data, stewardship and governance arrangements and agree an action plan for the firm
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines practical frameworks with case studies, group exercises and templates, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's business model.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of risk, compliance, investment or reporting in a regulated firm is helpful. No specialist sustainability background is required.
Core Reading: ISSB, IFRS S1 General Requirements and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures (2023)
TCFD, Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (2017)
IOSCO, Recommendations on Sustainability-Related Practices, Policies, Procedures and Disclosure in Asset Management (2021)
TNFD, Recommendations of the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (2023)

modules.title: Climate and ESG Risk Management
modules.summary: How physical and transition risks and wider ESG factors become credit, market, operational, liquidity and reputational risks, and how to integrate them into the firm's risk framework.
objectives: Explain physical and transition risk transmission channels
Integrate climate and ESG risks into the risk taxonomy and appetite
Assess materiality of climate risk for the firm's business model
syllabus: Physical and transition risks and their transmission channels
Climate risk in credit, market, operational and liquidity risk
Materiality assessment and risk appetite
Basel Committee and IAIS expectations for climate risk

modules.title: Climate Scenario Analysis and Stress Testing
modules.summary: Using climate scenarios to explore the resilience of the firm's business model and portfolios, and turning results into decisions.
objectives: Explain the design and use of NGFS climate scenarios
Apply scenario analysis to portfolios and the business model
Translate scenario results into risk management and strategy
syllabus: NGFS scenarios: orderly, disorderly and hot house world
Time horizons, data gaps and modelling limitations
Portfolio and business model scenario analysis
Using results in capital planning and strategy

modules.title: Transition Plans
modules.summary: Designing a transition plan that sets credible targets, links them to business strategy and capital allocation, and can be monitored and evidenced.
objectives: Explain the components of a credible transition plan
Design targets, metrics and interim milestones
Assess the plan's credibility from a supervisor's and investor's perspective
syllabus: Transition plan frameworks and elements
Financed emissions, targets and interim milestones
Linking plans to strategy, products and capital allocation
Red flags of a non-credible transition plan

modules.title: Sustainability Disclosures
modules.summary: Preparing climate and sustainability disclosures aligned with ISSB standards and the TCFD architecture of governance, strategy, risk management and metrics.
objectives: Explain the structure of ISSB-style sustainability disclosures
Apply governance, strategy, risk management and metrics and targets requirements
Design controls and assurance over sustainability reporting
syllabus: The ISSB standards and the TCFD four-pillar architecture
Scope 1, 2 and 3 and financed emissions
Connectivity with financial statements
Controls, data lineage and external assurance

modules.title: Product Labelling and Greenwashing
modules.summary: Making sustainability claims about products and the firm that are clear, fair and substantiated, and meeting product labelling and disclosure regimes.
objectives: Identify the forms of greenwashing and how supervisors detect them
Apply substantiation standards to sustainability claims and labels
Design product governance controls for sustainability-related products
syllabus: Greenwashing, greenhushing and misleading claims
Sustainable product labels and disclosure regimes
Substantiation, evidence and marketing review
Case studies of greenwashing enforcement

modules.title: ESG Data, Ratings and Methodologies
modules.summary: Understanding the limits of ESG data and ratings, assessing providers and building data governance fit for risk management and disclosure.
objectives: Assess the quality, coverage and comparability of ESG data
Evaluate ESG ratings methodologies and their limitations
Design data governance for sustainability data
syllabus: ESG data sources, gaps and estimation
Ratings divergence and methodology transparency
Due diligence on ESG data and ratings providers
IOSCO recommendations on ESG ratings and data providers

modules.title: Stewardship and Engagement
modules.summary: Using stewardship, engagement and voting to manage ESG risks and deliver sustainability commitments, and evidencing the outcomes achieved.
objectives: Design a stewardship policy aligned with the firm's sustainability commitments
Apply engagement, escalation and voting strategies
Evidence stewardship outcomes credibly
syllabus: Stewardship principles and policy design
Engagement priorities, escalation and collaborative engagement
Proxy voting and voting disclosure
Reporting stewardship activities and outcomes

modules.title: Governance of Sustainability and Capstone Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together around board oversight, accountability, remuneration and capability for sustainability, with a workshop in which participants assess their own firm.
objectives: Design governance and accountability for sustainability risks and commitments
Assess the board's capability to oversee sustainability matters
Produce a prioritised action plan for the firm's sustainability approach
syllabus: Board oversight, committees and management accountability
Remuneration links and sustainability capability
Seeing the firm the way a supervisor does: a sustainability self-assessment
Workshop: the firm's twelve-month sustainability action plan

related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms understand the quantum threat, build a cryptographic inventory, plan post-quantum migration and report readiness to the board and supervisors.

related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving industry professionals and their advisers a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks and controls that matter.
